classification.difficultyReason: Differentiate a cubic and use the sign of the derivative to decide whether it is one-to-one. Part a is a routine always-positive derivative. Part b needs the roots of 3x^2-12, a sign change, and a justification that the function is not one-to-one. The method is signposted, so this is a short linked procedure.

content.prompt:
Decide whether the inverse of each function is a function.

(You will need to differentiate to decide whether it is strictly increasing or decreasing).

answer.short: Yes. $f'(x)=3x^2+2>0$ for all real $x$, so $f$ is strictly increasing and its inverse is a function.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f'(x)&=3x^2+2\end{align*}$$
Since $x^2\geq0$, $f'(x)\geq2>0$ for every real $x$. Thus $f$ is strictly increasing throughout its domain and is one-to-one. Its inverse is therefore a function.

answer.short: No. $f'(x)<0$ for $-2<x<2$ and $f'(x)>0$ for $x>2$, so $f$ is not one-to-one. For example, $f(0)=f(2\sqrt3)=0$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f'(x)&=3x^2-12\\&=3(x-2)(x+2)\end{align*}$$
So $f'(x)<0$ for $-2<x<2$ and $f'(x)>0$ for $x>2$. The function is not strictly increasing or strictly decreasing, so it is not one-to-one.

For example, $f(0)=0$ and $f(2\sqrt3)=24\sqrt3-24\sqrt3=0$. Its inverse is not a function.
